Our Charcoal tint automotive films are non-reflective films that reduces glare and costly UV damage to your vehicles interior.
These auto-tint films can reject up to 50% of the suns total energy, acting as a sunscreen and helping protect passengers from the damaging effects of ultra violet.

People don't usually associate automotive window film with increased safety, but today's vehicles use tempered glass in the side and rear windows. An accident or a blow from a heavy object can cause these windows to shatter into hundreds of tiny sharp pieces of glass. Although automotive films are not sold as safety films, they can help hold broken glass together.
Can I use an automotive tint film on a building?

Unlike Architectural window tint films which are reflective and commonly seen on commercial buildings, Automotive tint films are non-reflective and therefore absorb energy from the sun. This absorption can lead to high levels of heat build up which is not a problem in a moving car but if used on flat glass, this absorption can lead to breakage. We therefore recommend that you check that you are using the correct film for the job.

We recommend these film to councils, government & schooling bodies including child minders, playgroups, crèches etc to upgrade the existing glass to safety standards. Once applied, this film will upgrade the glass to BS6260 Class B standards.

Designed to greatly reduce the hazards associated with breaking glass caused by vandalism, turbulent weather and forced entry this completely clear film will improve the shatter resistance of glass, holding the pieces firmly in place.
The film forms an almost invisible shield that holds glass shards intact when a pane breaks. These various levels of protection are available to address different hazard levels.

Reflective window films provide excellent ‘One Way Vision"" in daylight to stop those prying eyes. These films are the ideal choice for commercial buildings if trying to hide an unattractive combination of blinds, curtains and interior furnishings.
Reeded films create privacy by diffusing light and also helps to reject UV rays.
Reflective films also provide exceptional heat rejection, which in turn reduces the cost of air conditioning.

Note: Because the Solar Silver film work by reflecting light, it means that they have the reverse effect when it is dark at night or on a late afternoon in the winter. For the same reason this film is not recommended if you are trying to achieve privacy between two internal rooms.

column1: Most glitter films come with just a backing liner. Anyone familiar with the application of glitter vinyl will know that this can make them extremely tricky to apply, as using a squeegee to create a smooth and even application can create a horrible glittery mess. The use of an application tape to avoid this is pretty much out of the question. However, as well as a backing liner ASLAN has cleverly given SparkleColour a transparent top protective liner too which does the job of an application tape and allows for a much cleaner application. This also means the film is ideal for cad cutting, by cutting and weeding in reverse through the backing liner.

Unlike its rivals, the ASLAN SC123 is ideal for cad cutting. This is done by cutting and weeding in reverse through the backing liner and using the transparent top protective liner as an application tape.

For full surface coverage simply remove the backing liner and apply the Sparkle Colour to the surface easily using a squeegee. Once in position and squeegeed on, just remove the protective top liner - easy!
ASLAN Sparkle Colour is PVC Free and doesn't contain harmful VOC's. It is easy to apply and removes residue free from smooth flat surfaces.

column1: Paper application tapes are made from either standard or premium weight paper and coated with a special rubber based latex adhesive and are suitable for pretty much any application from signage, vehicle graphics and window graphics. They have the advantage that they can be torn by hand and are also suitable for both wet and dry application. The paper used is translucent when applied to the graphics so that positioning of the decals so much easier.

As a general rule, the larger the graphics are, the lower the tack level needs to be to transfer it successfully. So for very small intricate graphics it would be better to go to a higher tack level and conversely, for larger sized graphics a lower level of adhesion would be better. This rule is based on regular sign vinyl so exceptions to this would be if you are using a vinyl of film that has a high tack adhesive like reflective vinyl or a very low tack adhesive such as a stencil film. Then you would want to ensure that the level of adhesion is a closer match to the level of the vinyl underneath.
